bear_case: Hormuz reopening faces physical implementation challenges that oil markets are only beginning to price: Iran has laid approximately a dozen mines in the Strait, ship captains may take weeks to decide that safe passage is genuinely restored, and Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister confirmed Tehran will not begin implementation until the formal June 19 signing. If full tanker traffic restoration takes 4–6 weeks rather than days, the Brent decline from $87 to $83 may reverse partially toward $86–88 before the permanent oil price reset occurs — and any Brent bounce re-tests the $97 regime trigger thesis from the wrong direction. Meanwhile, the broader market is priced for perfection: SPX at 7,554 trades at 22.7x forward earnings with CME FedWatch pricing a 70% probability of at least one Fed hike by year-end 2026 — the most hawkish year-end pricing in this cycle. Warsh's first FOMC press conference on June 17 is 48 hours away; without the dot plot as a standard scaffolding tool, a single ambiguous sentence about inflation persistence could push the 30Y back to 5.05–5.20%, converting the Nasdaq's best day since March into a confirmed near-term top. A Warsh hawkish surprise combined with an Iran implementation slip — two individually non-trivial risks occurring simultaneously — sends SPX from 7,554 to 7,280–7,350 before Juneteenth, erasing the entire Iran deal premium. **Invalidation: If SPX closes above 7,460 for a second consecutive session on June 16 AND Warsh June 17 delivers neutral policy communication AND 30Y remains below 5.00% post-presser, BUY conviction upgrades to HIGH and TBT reduces by 50% — those are the two conditions that remain outstanding. If 30Y re-breaches 5.05% within 24 hours of the Warsh press conference AND SPX closes below 7,460, BUY reverts to HOLD immediately — do not wait for a weekly close.**
